Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:29: Nevertheless, the building of the soul is from the side of Chesed, which is the daughter of our father Abraham, as Rashbi explains (Mishpatim 95a), and therefore our father Abraham, peace be upon him, merited Chesed, because he was not sparing of his body or his money - for by nature it is hard for a person to give over his soul and body for the sanctification of the Name, since this is contrary to nature, and the flesh opposes it. So too giving one's money to charity, especially if he distributes a great deal, acting contrary to nature, becomes bound up with Chesed. From this the discerning reader may infer regarding all other matters of divine service that are contrary to nature, which must be done from love in order to merit Chesed - and this is the matter of the ten trials with which our father Abraham, peace be upon him, was tested, as explained in the passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:30: What they say, that "eternal love" is the lower world bound to the upper world without separation, and it says at the end, "blessed is He forever and to all eternity," seems to me that the sum of these words can be understood together with what is explained in the Tikkunim (Chadash 100b), which I have in manuscript - his words: "the elder arose and took a stone in his hands, opened and said: holy candle, until now the stone was in your hand; from now on it has ascended among the upper beings - guard yourself from her stones, for she ascends through the mouths of the righteous, in their prayers to her husband, and in their deeds. For this stone, when it descends below, is the 'testing stone' [concerning which it is said (Psalms 11:5) 'the Lord'] tests the righteous, and by it the Patriarchs were tested, and therefore it is said (ibid. 118:22) 'the stone the builders rejected' - these being the Patriarchs. And when it descends below, it descends in the manner of David, and when it ascends, it is said of it, 'the stone the builders rejected has become the head cornerstone,' in the manner of YHVH; by it Abraham was tested with ten trials, and at the time a person is tested by it, it is lowered, and afterward, once he stands firm in her trial, it ascends with him to her husband, who is YHVH; at that time the person ascends with it above all those levels and appointees by which a person is tested. And when Samael saw that permission was given for every righteous person to have a trial, and saw that he [Mordechai] stood firm in it, he said, 'and all this avails me nothing' [Esther 5:13] - and if you say this was said of Mordechai by Haman, certainly Haman was a counterpart of Samael, in whom he was clothed, and the ten lower crowns were clothed in his ten sons; and because he stood firm in the trial, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave it into his hand - how much more so one who is tested for the sake of the Shechinah in exile, since ten treasures of the Name of the Crown descend upon her, which are Yud-Heh, Vav-Heh, being sefirot full of the treasures that surround the supernal Crown of the King and the Matronita; and this is the supernal Crown of which it is said, on the Sabbath day, in the Kedusha, 'a crown they shall give You, O Lord our God'" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:31: Further, the matter of love is explained (Zohar, Ki Tisa 190b) - his words: "the Torah contains love, brotherhood, and truth: Abraham loves Isaac, Isaac loves Abraham, embracing one another. Jacob - both hold to him in love and brotherhood, giving him their spirits, one to another."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:32: Rashbi, peace be upon him, teaches us the secret of the essence of love, and the matter is what he said above this, concerning the love among the colleagues: "all the colleagues in the days of Rabbi Shimon had a love of soul and spirit between them." This matter is explained thus: a person's love for his fellow is through the soul, for the desire of the soul is love, and although the bodies are divided and separated one from another, the soul of this one and that one is spiritual, and spirituality is not separated but unified in the ultimate unity; and when one colleague's soul arouses its desire to love his fellow, his fellow's soul is also aroused and he loves him, and the two souls become one, as the verse says concerning David and Jonathan (I Samuel 18:1) "and the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul" - and David's love for Jonathan showed his love for him, as it says (ibid. 20:41) "and they kissed one another and wept... until David exceeded," and so he said at his passing (II Samuel 1:26) "your love to me was more wonderful than the love of women."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:33: The reality that souls become bound one to another through the arousal of love, Solomon the king, peace be upon him, teaches us by saying (Proverbs 27:19) "as in water, face answers to face, so the heart of man to man" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Yalkut, 961): Rabbi Chanina said, does water have a face? Rather, just as with this water, when you put it in a vessel and gaze at it, your own face is seen in it, so the heart of man to man - so far. This is explained in what is said there: just as with water in a vessel, when a person gazes at it, he sees his own face in it, and there are two kinds of "faces" - the face he gazes with, which is direct light, and the face in the water, which he sees as reflected light returning from below, from the water in the vessel, up to him - the two faces are one, joined as one; and if a person withdraws his gaze from the water, nothing at all is seen in the water, for if there is no direct light, there is no reflected light. So it is with the heart of man to man - when a person arouses the desire of his heart to love his fellow, that desire arouses the desire of his fellow's heart toward him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:34: Although we said that the face a person gazes at in the water is the direct light, this is according to physical reality; but in spiritual reality, this is the secret of the arousal from below that ascends from our deeds to the Shechinah, and this is the matter of "female waters" mentioned in the Zohar (Bereishit 18a); and if there is no arousal from below, there is no arousal from above, as it is said (Genesis 2:6) "and a mist went up from the earth," and afterward "and it watered," as is explained in the Zohar, portion of Bereishit (35a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:35: To understand the words of the parable applied to its moral in all their particulars: just as, when a person gazes at water so that his face is seen there, two things are needed - water and a vessel - and if either is lacking, no face is seen at all, so soul and heart are needed. It is already explained in the Tikkunim in several places (70b) that the soul dwells in the heart - the heart is the vessel and the soul is the water in the vessel, for a heart without a soul is like a vessel without water. And just as gazing at water, if there is no vessel, nothing will be seen, because the vessel, being coarse, is what causes that form to reflect back - for water is simple, and because of its simplicity, the form appearing in it passes right through unless something blocks the form, like a polished mirror, which, if there is no thick backing behind it to block the form, the form passes through it and a person sees nothing - so a person acquires no love in the soul of a person he has never seen the form of, so that when his love for him is aroused, his fellow's love for him will be aroused too. The gazing of faces in the water is the arousal of love aroused from the desire of the soul in one's heart toward the soul in his fellow's heart, and then the two souls become bound in a single bond of love, even though they are distant one from another, for the waters, which are the souls, being fine and spiritual, all portions of God above, have no separation between them, even though they are in separate vessels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:36: This is like the inner essence of the Godhead, within the sapphire vessel, whose inner essence is entirely one, unified, although the vessels change; you already know that Ra'aya Meheimna compared (end of Bo, 42b) the inner essence to water spreading within vessels - that if the vessels break, the water returns to its source and they all become a single source again, as they were before the spreading. The aspect of direct light and reflected light, which are "face to face," I shall not explain, since I rely on what my teacher, peace be upon him, has explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:37: Now, with this introduction we understand what the passage says - "in love and brotherhood they give their spirits, one to another" - for the binding of the [divine] attributes together in this love is through their inner spirit, since from the aspect of vessels they are separate vessels for their actions - this one Chesed, this one Din, this one mercy - but through the spirit, which is one, as it is written (see Ecclesiastes 3:19) "and they all have one spirit," they are bound and "give their spirits, one to another."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:38: Incidentally, we learn from the parable "as in water, face answers to face" that it is impossible for a person, wishing to cleave to his Maker in the secret of love, to cleave to Him in His aspect before Atzilut, for that aspect is hidden and has no grasp of love within it - similar to the parable we gave, that a person cannot love a soul without any depiction of a body, even though there is, God forbid, no body above; the intent is regarding the reality of the revelation of His actions to us, similar to the soul, which reveals its actions - before it is clothed in a body, it has no action. So too it is explained (in Ra'aya Meheimna there) - their words: "before He created an image in the world and depicted a form, He was singular, without form or likeness; and whoever recognizes Him as He was before creation, who is outside of image, it is forbidden to make Him a form or image in the world, neither with the letter Heh nor with the letter Yud, nor even with the holy Name, nor with any letter or point in the world" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:39: If a person's soul cleaves, it is in the secret of the supernal life spreading within the vessels, which are His holy Names - and this is (Deuteronomy 4:4) "but you who cleave to YHVH your God are all alive today" - meaning, they cleave to the eternal Living One, blessed be He, who cleaves to His Name, for He and His Name are entirely one; YHVH is His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:40: When a person cleaves to his Maker with complete love, from his heart and his soul, so he causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to cleave to him, similar to the "face answers to face" in water that I explained. So too Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Terumah 162a) - his words: "'and you shall love' - this is the beginning of the right, to love the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of cleaving to Him; and what is this 'right'? This arouses love - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, arouses His right toward him and He receives him with love. All the affairs of the world depend only on desire - spirit draws spirit and brings spirit - and the sign of this is (Job 34:14) 'if He should set His heart upon him, He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul.' When a person arouses love toward the Holy One, blessed be He, the arousal of the right is aroused only through three colors, as it says (Deuteronomy 6:5) 'with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might' - here are three colors, lest you say 'either this or that,' for it is not written 'either with all your heart or with all your soul or with all your might,' but rather all are needed - heart and soul and money. And then the Holy One, blessed be He, arouses His right toward him and stretches it out to him and receives him; and therefore it is written (Psalms 110:1) 'the Lord says to my master, sit at My right hand' - and this is the secret of this verse, which we have already touched upon, that David the king spoke of his own level, when he is bound to the right" - so far. Our intent in this passage is clear: he says that when a person gives over his spirit to love the Name, he thereby causes the Name to love him and cleave to him - this is what he means by "spirit draws spirit and brings spirit" - meaning, when a person arouses his spirit toward the Name, so the Name's spirit is drawn toward him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:41: Along these lines, Rabbi Yosi himself, the author of this very passage, explains, in the portion of Korach, the verse (Job 34:14) "if He should set His heart upon him, He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul" - that the intent concerns one who performs levirate marriage with his brother's wife: "if He should set" [his heart] upon him means toward the soul of his brother, bringing there his heart, meaning his intent; "his spirit and his soul He would gather to Himself" - by his good intent he draws the soul of the deceased and it is rebuilt through him; if not, it is not rebuilt. These are Rashbi's words (Zohar, Korach 177a): "'if He should set His heart upon him' - this person who is commanded to build the building [through levirate marriage] must direct his heart and desire toward that deceased one; from this we learn that a person who comes upon that woman for the sake of her beauty and desire, the building of the world is not built, for desire and heart were not directed toward the deceased; and therefore it is written 'if He should set His heart upon him' with the desire of the heart, directed toward him - then 'his spirit and his soul He would gather to Him' and it is drawn to him" - so far, as relevant to us. Here it is explicitly stated that the spirit of the living and his intent draws another spirit in this world, and similarly for the matter of intent in love - that when a person sets his heart and soul and money in the yearning of love for his Maker, he thereby causes a supernal, divine spirit to be drawn upon him - namely, the Holy One, blessed be He, stretches out His right hand toward him and receives him. The matter of "and receives him" will be explained to you in chapter 3, in the secret of the kisses of the lovers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:42: Further, this matter of love is explained at the end of the words of the Sabba (Mishpatim 114a), where Rabbi Chiya says there, on the verse (Song of Songs 8:6) "set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm" - the matter of the love and bond of Knesset Yisrael with the Holy One, blessed be He - and says afterward: "we have love and the sparks of the fire of the heart after You; may it be Your will that our image be engraved in Your heart, just as Your image is engraved in our hearts" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:43: From this the discerning reader will discern the matter of the love of the Lord: that when a person constantly engraves the depiction of the Name YHVH in his heart, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 16:8) "I have set the Lord before me always," he thereby causes the depiction of his soul to be engraved above, and the Creator, blessed be He, will love him - and this is the matter of "as in water, face answers to face" that I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:44: The end of the verse, "so the heart of man" - along the secret way - just as it is according to the plain sense I explained above, so it is exactly along the hint above: when a person arouses his heart to love the Lord, he is called "Adam" in the secret of Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh, which sums to "Adam" [numerically], for YHVH will love him and be bound to him, as it is written (I Chronicles 28:9) "if you seek Him, He will be found by you" - for one must always initiate the arousal from below; this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Pinchas 241a) concerning falling on one's face [in prayer], saying: then "Adam," who is the image comprising all the rest, lowers himself and stirs his face and turns aside his own being and spirit toward the "Adam" engraved upon those images, to arouse it toward himself as is fitting - and this is (Psalms 25:1) "to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul" - so far. When you scrutinize his words, that he says "to arouse it toward himself," you will find our words align with his, and from this we learn the secret of love applicable to all other matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:45: Here it is explained, in this chapter, the essence of the matter of love: that its reality is the bond and union of cause and effect, one with another, through their inner soul; and so too a person cannot love the Name and cleave to Him except through his soul, that is, "with all your soul," as we shall explain; and this is the word "ahavah" [love] - meaning "cleaving" [dveikut], as it says (Deuteronomy 30:20) "to love the Lord," etc., "and to cleave to Him" - for through love he cleaves to Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:46: There are further particulars concerning the essence of the matter of love, to be explained in a separate chapter, in order to give some breathing space between chapters:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:1: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Va'etchanan 267b) that the whole of Atzilut is called love - his words: "come and see, everything is called love, and through love everything stands, as it is written (Song of Songs 8:7) 'many waters cannot quench the love,' and everything stands in love, for so the holy Name is found - for they have established, the Yud, the point [tip] above, is never separated from the Yud forever, since love rests upon it and is never separated from it. The Heh - they have already established that the Yud is never separated from it, and they are found together in affection, not separated one from another, Yud-Heh; and it has been said, as it is written (Genesis 2:10) 'and a river goes out from Eden' - going out forever in affection, cleaving one to another. The Vav is always the bridegroom to the bride, whose way is in affection - Yud in Heh, Heh with Vav, Vav with Heh; therefore everything is called love, and one is bound to the other in affection, and therefore whoever loves the King is bound in that love, and therefore 'and you shall love the Lord your God'" - so far. Here it is explicitly explained that the whole of Atzilut is termed by the word "love."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:2: Now, this presents a difficulty for what was explained in the previous chapter, that love in particular is ascribed to Chesed, as is also explained above, from this same passage we quoted (267b): "'and you shall love' - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with Chesed on all sides."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:3: In the Tikkunim (Zohar Chadash 101a), love is explained in Binah, so it seems its root is there - his words, concerning fear and love: "in this manner, whoever fears the Holy One, blessed be He, the Yud rests, entering his heart; and whoever loves Him, the Heh rests in his brain. Concerning these two letters it is said, 'the hidden things' - for whoever fears the Holy One, blessed be He, or loves Him, is hidden from human beings; and 'the revealed things' are Vav-Heh - whoever occupies himself with Torah, the Vav rests in his mouth, and whoever occupies himself with mitzvah, the Heh rests in his two hundred and forty-eight limbs" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:4: In these words, fear is also explained in the Zohar (Naso 122b) - that this is the Yud that is upon a person's head, and from it fear enters a person's heart, to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and to guard himself from transgressing the negative commandments. The Heh, Love, is upon a person's head, and from it the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, enters his two hundred and forty-eight limbs, to fulfill the positive commandments with them. The Vav is upon a person's head, and from it enters into a person's mouth the words to teach in Torah - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:5: What appears to resolve these passages is that there is a distinction between the reality of love as a person loves the Holy One, blessed be He, and the reality of love above, in Atzilut - for the reality of love in Atzilut, all of Atzilut is called love, since love means the bond and union of cause and effect, one with another, as I explained in the previous chapter, and therefore all of Atzilut is unified in its parts in a complete bond and union, so love applies rightly to the whole of it as one. But from where does love flow to man? This Rashbi further teaches us: that from the side of the supernal Heh, love flows to him to fulfill the mitzvot with yearning, as we shall explain the reason.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:6: Once a person merits loving the King and fulfilling the mitzvot with yearning, causing the bond and union of the attributes, called love, he then merits the right, called love, which I explained in the previous chapter is called love because of the bond of the left within the right; and this is precise in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, when he says, "'and you shall love' - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with Chesed on all sides" - meaning, from all the aspects and completeness of Chesed, and the completeness of Chesed is the comprising of Gevurah within it, and a person merits it only by giving over his body, soul, and money in love of his Maker, like Abraham.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:7: That which causes Chesed and Din to be bound certainly causes all the attributes to be bound as one; and although we say that the lover merits the right, the intent is not to the right arm alone, but he merits all the attributes together, since they are all flowing from Chesed, and from the side of Chesed the ten sefirot are unified, as we say (Sotah 47a) "the right draws near," and "and the bones came together, bone to its bone" (Ezekiel 37:7), and it is explained in the Tikkunim (105b) that this verse refers to the reality of union, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:8: Proof that the sefirot's nearness and union is from the side of Chesed: the two hundred and forty-eight positive commandments are from the side of Chesed, as is explained in the Tikkunim, which we shall quote below, and every mitzvah is the union of the whole of Atzilut, which is YHVH; and it is already explained in the Tikkunim (73a) and in Ra'aya Meheimna (see Pinchas 228b) that a mitzvah is truly YHVH, for Mem-Tzadi is Yud-Heh in the At-Bash cipher; and the term "mitzvot" means union, along the lines of (Berachot 6b) "the whole world was created only for the sake of union" [tzavta, related to mitzvah] - meaning, God, called Chesed, as is explained in the portion of Vayikra (23b), and likewise in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar), that Chesed is a God who unifies Vav-Heh; and along these lines (Psalms 42:9) "by day the Lord commands His kindness" - Chesed is called "day," comprising all the days, and Chesed builds with everyone and unifies them, along the lines of (ibid. 89:3) "I said, the world shall be built with kindness." This is what it says there, "is crowned with Chesed on all sides" - meaning, in all the directions, and does everything with Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:9: This is likewise said in the same portion, concerning the four compartments of the tefillin (Zohar, Va'etchanan 262b) - his words: "the third [compartment], 'Hear, O Israel' - 'Israel' the elder - 'and you shall love the Lord your God' - we learn, Rabbi Shimon [taught], this is a supernal secret: Israel is crowned on the side of Abba, and what is it? Abraham; and he is crowned on the side of Imma, and what is it? Isaac. We learn, 'and you shall love' - because he loves the King, he does extra kindness with everyone; and this extra kindness is called 'the kindness of truth' [chesed shel emet], which requires no reward, but is done only out of the love of the King, who loves him greatly; and upon the love of the King depends Chesed - and this is the third compartment" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:10: Here it is explained that the lover causes the spreading of Chesed in the world, as it writes, "because he loves Him greatly, kindness increases in the world." As for what it says, that Israel is crowned on the side of Abba, this is understood together with what is explained in the Idra of Ha'azinu (291a), concerning the two crowns hidden in Abba and Imma, with which they crown him. And it may be that this matter is brought in here to explain the phrase "the Lord your God," for YHVH is called such from the side of the crown of Abba, and "your God" [Elohecha] from the side of the crown of Imma. Or it may be that the crowns are alluded to by the added word "et" [before "the Lord"]. The first seems to me the primary interpretation, and "et" is the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:11: As for what it says, that the true service, in the matter of love, is one who does not serve in order to receive a reward, and this is the one who merits Chesed - the reason is that one who serves in order to receive a reward is necessarily bound to the side of Gevurah, for according to the measure of his service, he will be bestowed upon according to strict judgment and precise reckoning; but one who serves not in order to receive a reward, since his service is without measure, not waiting for a known portion of reward, so he is given without measure, from the side of Chesed, since Chesed bestows without measure, and then he is bound in love. Therefore, since he does not serve to receive a reward but from complete love, he causes the crown of Gevurah to be comprised beneath the crown of Chesed, and the acts of kindness spread through all the directions, since Chesed spreads through the world, and the building of the whole world is with Chesed, without any kindness having preceded it - but rather, out of His way of goodness, to do good and give to both the wicked and the good, without being exacting with any creature; and it is the way of the attribute of Chesed to love, to give, and to desire, for from the love it has for causes and all creatures, it bestows from its Chesed, without receiving from them any arousal on account of which it bestows upon them. So one who loves the King performs an act of kindness with the King, and this kindness is to perform the service and not hope for the reward of the service, in the pattern of the attribute of Chesed - and through this he is bound to the attribute of Chesed and increases kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:12: He explains, in brief words, the matter of love, saying, "but only because of the love of the King, who loves him greatly" - the meaning being that the love of the King is so firmly fixed in his heart that there is nothing in the world he loves more than the King, and this is "who loves him greatly" - more than all the things in the world; and therefore he does not serve in order to receive a reward, for then he would be found serving and loving for the sake of the reward, and not from the side of love of the King. And even if he loves both the reward and the King, nevertheless it is not fitting that any reward be considered equal in value to the love of the King, in such a way that no created thing in the world, even the reward of the World to Come, should be loved by him more than the Holy One, blessed be He; rather, the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, exceeds everything - and therefore the merit of one who serves in this manner is rewarded without measure or limit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:13: As is explained (Zohar, Va'etchanan 267a) - their words: "'and you shall love' - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, and is crowned with Chesed on all sides, does kindness with everyone and is not sparing of his body or his money. From where do we learn this? From Abraham, as has been said - for he was not sparing, out of love of his Master, of his heart (that is, his inclination), or of his soul, or of his money. 'Of his heart' - he did not heed his own desire because of love of his Master; 'of his soul, his son, and his wife' - because of love of his Master; 'of his money' - for he sat at the crossroads and prepared food for the whole world; therefore he was crowned with the crown of Chesed, as it is written (Micah 7:20) 'kindness to Abraham' - and whoever is bound in love of his Master merits this. And not only this, but all the worlds are blessed because of him - this is [the meaning of] (Psalms 145:10) 'and Your pious ones shall bless You' - do not read 'yevarechuchah' but 'yevarechu Kaf-Heh' [they shall bless the Kaf-Heh, alluding to a secret pairing]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:14: One day Rabbi Yosi fell ill; Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Yitzchak, and Rabbi Yehudah came to visit him; they saw that he had fallen on his face and was sleeping; they sat down. When he awoke, they saw that his face was smiling; Rabbi Abba said to him, "you saw something new." He said to him, "certainly - for just now my soul ascended and saw the glory of those who gave themselves over for the sanctification of their Master, who were entering into thirteen mountains of pure balsam, and the Holy One, blessed be He, was delighting in them; and I saw what they did not give me permission to speak of, and I asked them, whose is this glory? They said to me, of those who love their Master, in that world; and from what I saw, my soul and heart were illuminated, and therefore my face is smiling."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:15: Rabbi Abba said to him, "happy is your portion, but the Torah already testifies concerning them, as it is written (Isaiah 64:3) 'no eye has seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for one who waits for Him.'" Rabbi Yehudah said to him, "the colleagues have already asked, this verse says 'yaaseh' [will do, future tense] - should it not say 'taaseh' [You will do]?" He said to him, "this has already been established, but the secret of the matter is what is written (Psalms 27:4) 'to behold the pleasantness of the Lord, and to visit His Temple' - and it has been established, 'the pleasantness of the Lord' is that which comes from the Holy Ancient One, in whom the Holy One, blessed be He, delights, for that pleasantness issues from the Ancient One; here too, 'no eye has seen, O God, besides You, will do' - who is this? The concealed Ancient One of all, for it all depends upon Him." He said to him, "certainly, this is so. Happy is the portion of those who cleave through the love of their Master - for these, there is no measure to their portion in that world."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:16: Rabbi Yitzchak said: how many chambers upon chambers do the righteous have in that world, and the highest chamber of all is for those who are bound through the love of their Master, for their dwelling is bound to everything and rises above everything. Why? Because the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with this - come and see, everything is called love, etc. - quoted at the beginning of this chapter - so far. Here is explained the merit of one who serves from love, that he merits the supernal pleasantness which no eye has seen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:17: I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, a more explicit reason for the merit of one who serves from love: one who serves from love of the King of the world, not for hope of reward in this world nor for hope of reward in the World to Come, but from love alone - the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself is the One who pays his reward. For if he acts for the sake of the reward of this world, so that he have wealth and children, behold, he receives his reward in this world, and just as this world perishes and is lost, so his reward perishes and is lost in this world; and if he acts for the sake of the Garden of Eden, his reward is through the world of angels serving the Garden. But if he acts for the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, he binds his soul to the Infinite and to His attributes, to unify them properly, and therefore his reward is from the very highest, "to behold the pleasantness of the Lord."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:18: It appears to me, to explain this matter further, that each person, according to his deeds, merits accordingly in the future: if he merited the nefesh alone, his rest is in the place of souls in the courtyard of death; if he merited the ruach, he merits the Garden of Eden; and if he merited the neshamah, he merits ascending to the supernal Garden of Eden - and those who merit the neshamah are called "lovers," as Rashbi explains (Vayigash 206a), "to cause those who love Me to inherit substance" (Proverbs 8:21) - these are those in whom the holy soul dwells, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:19: What is written, "for their dwelling is bound to everything" - the meaning is that each and every chamber in the Garden of Eden draws from a particular attribute and is bound to that attribute according to the mitzvah he performed; but the chamber of the pious is a chamber that draws from the whole of Atzilut and is bound to all of it, because he caused the unification of the whole of Atzilut, as explained, and "rises above everything" - the reality of this chamber is above all the other chambers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:20: The pious Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, peace be upon him, writes on the Mishnah (Avot 1:3) "do not be like servants who serve in order to receive a reward," and likewise on the Mishnah (ibid. 5:16) "any love that is dependent on something" - matters needed for love - and therefore I have chosen to quote some of them, essential to the discourse we are engaged in.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:21: He writes on the Mishnah "do not be" - his words: our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Pesachim 50b): it is written (Psalms 57:11) "for Your kindness is great unto the heavens," and it is written (ibid. 108:5) "for Your kindness is great above the heavens" - this is no contradiction: here it refers to those who act for its own sake, etc. - for one who acts for its own sake cleaves to the Name, blessed be He, and there is no limit to the giving of his reward; but those who believe in the Name, blessed be He, that He rewards and punishes, and occupy themselves with His commandments more [for that reason], their reward is fixed, up to the heavens. And know that the great and awesome day of the Lord is above the heavens, and the discerning will understand. To this David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:159) "see how I have loved Your precepts, O Lord; revive me according to Your kindness" - for I am among those who act for its own sake, therefore I ask from the treasury that has no limit, which is Your great kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:22: To this the prophet said (Lamentations 3:21-24) "this I recall to my mind, therefore I have hope: the kindnesses of the Lord, that they are not consumed... they are new every morning... 'the Lord is my portion,' says my soul, 'therefore I will hope in Him.'" One may explain what this thing is that he recalled to his mind, and what his soul said. The matter, as I see it, is that a person, being human, finds it hard to conceive of service without receiving a reward, and this is possible only for the soul, by virtue of its own nature, since it is from the upper beings and desires, by nature, to serve like the angels above; and people whose humanity has returned entirely to being soul-like are those who serve without receiving a reward. Therefore he says, to his heart, in the aspect that is human, he says words that settle in the heart; but to his soul he need not say arguments, for it says of itself that it chooses service for its own sake, and not for any other reason - and this is what he says, "'the Lord is my portion,' says my soul, therefore I will hope in Him" - from a different argument.
